wu: Flashcard Race: Show room flashcards (kitchen, bedroom, bathroom, living room) one by one; students shout the room name and make a sentence like 'It's big!'
wuAlt: Simon Says: Play Simon Says with prepositions, e.g., 'Simon says stand in the bedroom'
Miming Game: Students mime activities (e.g., cooking) and others guess the room
pres: Use a big house poster; point to each room and model 'This is the kitchen. It is big. Where is the fridge? It is in the kitchen.'; ask students to repeat and point to objects in the poster
presAlt: Story Time: Read a short story about a family in their house, highlighting room names and prepositions
Realia Tour: Bring toy furniture; place items in 'rooms' on a mat and ask 'Where is the bed?'
prac: House Map Pairs: Give each pair a blank house map with rooms; one student places furniture flashcards, the other asks 'Where is the table?' and answers 'It is in the kitchen.'
pracAlt: Bingo Game: Students draw a house grid and write room names; call out 'Find the bathroom!' and mark off
Flashcard Swap: Students pass room flashcards and say 'I have the kitchen. It is small.'
ls: Listen and Draw: Play an audio describing a dream house (e.g., 'There is a big bedroom and a small bathroom'); students draw the rooms and objects as they hear them
re: Room Relay: Divide students into teams; run to the board, write a room name, and run back; first team to write 4 rooms wins
prod: Dream House Roleplay: In pairs, one student describes their dream house using 'There is/are + big/small', the other draws it; present to the class
rw: Read and Match: Students read short descriptions (e.g., 'I sleep here. It is small.') and match them to room pictures; then write 3 sentences about their own house
st: Story: Read 'The Magic House' story about a house with different rooms; end with the Goodbye Song, sticker chart, and high-five line
g: Teacher hides toy furniture; students ask 'Where is the bed?' and hunt for it
Students mime room activities (e.g., brushing teeth) and others guess
Students assemble a house puzzle and name each room
Call out 'Jump in the bedroom!' and students hop to the correct flashcard
One student describes a room, others draw it
diff: Fast finishers: Write 5 sentences about their dream house with adjectives
Support: Use sentence starters like 'There is a ____ in the ____.'
hw: Read the 'My House' page in your mini-book and circle 3 new words
Draw your dream house and label 2 rooms
Ask your family about their house and write 2 sentences
tip: Use Moroccan home elements (e.g., riad, courtyard) to connect the theme to students' lives; praise effort, not accuracy, to build confidence
